title: Investing, Gambling or Scam?
subtitle: Twelve offers land on your phone. Sort each one into a bucket, then see the signs that give it away.
open.hint: Sort 12 offers and learn the red flags.
intro.title: Three buckets
intro.investing: Investing: you own or lend something real, and the returns are uncertain.
intro.gambling: Gambling: the outcome is mostly chance, with nothing of real value behind it.
intro.scam: Scam: someone lies about the returns or about how it works.
intro.last: Last time you sorted {right} of {total} correctly. Can you beat it?
tell.unregistered: Not registered with the market regulator
tell.honest_risk: Honest that you can lose money
tell.real_value: You own or lend something real
card.s1.text: A betting app where you win or lose money on the result of a cricket match.
card.s1.why: The result is decided by chance, and nothing of real value stands behind your money. That is gambling.
card.s2.text: A mix of many companies, held for years. The seller says plainly that it can fall.
card.s2.why: You own real companies, and the seller is honest about the risk. That is investing, with no promise of a gain.
card.s3.text: "Guaranteed 30% a month! Zero risk! Join today!"
card.s3.why: Nobody can guarantee a return like that. A huge promise with no risk is the classic sign of a scam.
card.s4.text: A stranger writes: "Only 2 spots left. Send money today and tell no one."
card.s4.why: Rushing you and asking you to keep quiet are tricks to stop you thinking or asking. That is a scam.
card.s5.text: A bond from a city water company. It promises 7% a year and explains that the company could fail to pay.
card.s5.why: You lend to a real business, and the risk is explained. It is investing, even though the rate is promised.
card.s6.text: A group that pays you for every friend you bring in. There is no product to buy.
card.s6.why: The money comes from new members, not from anything real. That is a pyramid scheme, and it must collapse.
card.s7.text: A hyped coin everyone is talking about. It doubled this week, and people say it will double again.
card.s7.why: This is speculation: a bet on price moves with little real value behind it. It is not always a scam, but it is not investing.
card.s8.text: A paid chat group that says it has secret tips that never lose.
card.s8.why: No tip never loses, and secrecy is a red flag. Paying for a promise like this is a scam.
card.s9.text: A savings plan from a registered fund company. It shows a range of results and its yearly fees.
card.s9.why: The seller is registered, shows fees, and gives a range instead of a promise. That is investing.
card.s10.text: An online game where you pay for a spin, and the prize is picked by chance.
card.s10.why: You pay for a chance and own nothing. That is gambling.
card.s11.text: A video of a celebrity: "I put my savings in this scheme and got rich. You can too!"
card.s11.why: A famous face is not proof, and the scheme names no registered seller. That is a scam.
card.s12.text: A seller who is registered with the market regulator. They explain fees and say returns can be negative.
card.s12.why: They are registered, open about fees, and honest about losses. That is investing.
done.title: How you did
done.missed: Red flags to watch for next time:
done.perfect: You spotted every one. Real offers can be harder to read, so keep asking the same questions.
check.title: Check what you learned
check.x1.prompt: A scheme promises {weekly} every week. Without compounding, how much is that over {weeks} weeks? Type a percentage.
check.x1.hint: Multiply the weekly rate by the number of weeks.
check.x1.explain: {weekly} a week for {weeks} weeks is {yearly} a year. Nothing real pays that.
check.x2.prompt: "Only 2 spots left. Send money today and tell no one." Which red flags are these?
check.x2.opt.a: Pressure to act now, and secrecy
check.x2.opt.b: A registered seller and honest risk
check.x2.opt.d: None, this is a normal offer
check.x2.fb.c: That offer made no promise of a return. The flags here are the hurry and the secrecy.
check.x2.hint: Which words push you to hurry, and which ask you to hide it?
check.x2.explain: Hurrying you and asking you to keep it secret are classic red flags.
check.x3.prompt: What is the main difference between investing and gambling?
check.x3.opt.a: Investing owns or lends something real. Gambling is mostly chance with no real value behind it
check.x3.opt.b: Investing is any bet on a price going up
check.x3.opt.c: Gambling always loses and investing always wins
check.x3.fb.b: A bet on a price move with little behind it is speculation, which is closer to gambling than to investing.
check.x3.hint: Think about what you own or lend in each case.
check.x3.explain: Investing has something real behind it. Gambling is mostly chance.
check.x4.prompt: A scheme pays you to bring in friends. What is true?
check.x4.opt.a: It needs endless new members, so it must collapse and most people lose
check.x4.opt.b: Recruiting friends is a normal way to earn income
check.x4.opt.c: It is safe because friends trust each other
check.x4.opt.d: It pays more the later you join
check.x4.fb.b: Earning mainly from recruiting is a red flag. The money comes from new members, not from real value.
check.x4.hint: Remember the pyramid lab: the numbers grow faster than any town.
check.x4.explain: The numbers outgrow any town, so a recruiting scheme must collapse.
